title: M & B Engineering Ltd - 544470 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: M&B Engineering FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR1,259.7 crores, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% on forex loss and steel/freight costs; no margin guidance given.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew 27% to INR1,260 crores and PAT rose 20% to INR92.6 crores, but Q4 revenue (INR364 crores, +16%) saw EBITDA flat at INR43 crores and margin down to 11.9% from 14%. Management attributed the margin squeeze to a INR3.9 crore Q4 forex loss (mostly unrealised translation), a 20%+ jump in domestic steel prices, and sharply higher export freight after the Iran conflict; it says adjusted EBITDA excluding forex is about 13%. Volume growth in Phenix was only about 8% in Q4 versus an expected ~15%, due to raw material and gas disruptions in March. Management guided top-line growth of 23-25% for FY27 but declined to give margin guidance.

segments.name: Phenix (PEB)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR985 crores, +29%; export revenue INR165.6 crores. Order book INR871 crores, of which export INR279 crores (32%). Sanand plant utilisation ~75-76% in FY26.

segments.name: Proflex (self-supported roofing)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR275 crores, +23%. Order book INR212 crores. One new unit from UAE commissioned January 2026; two US units expected Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at around 25%; management later cited a 23-25% range, and 20-25% volume growth in PEB and Proflex.
No EBITDA margin guidance for FY27: management cited steel price volatility, uncertain freight, FX and the conflict; will reassess after at least one more quarter.
FY27 export target about INR275-300 crores (around 10,000 tons vs 7,400 tons in FY26); export EBITDA expected 16-17% vs 10-11% domestic at current cost structure.
H1 FY27 expected softer due to Q1 labour availability and Q2 monsoon; H2 historically stronger.
FY27 capex about INR100 crores, including Sanand expansion, part Cheyyar expansion (H2) and maintenance capex.
US sectoral tariff reduced by 25% (effective 6 April per management); benefit partly shared with customers under contract clauses.
capex_capacity: Sanand: adding about 20,000 MT, commissioning expected Q2 FY27, taking capacity to 92,000 MTPA; utilisation expected 65-68% after expansion, peak 75%.
Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu): FY26 utilisation 50-55%; target 68-70% in FY27, with 75% as peak; expansion planned to be operational Q1 or Q2 FY28.
Proflex: installed capacity to rise by about 200,000 sq m p.a. once two US units are commissioned in Q2 FY27.
Volume targets FY27: PEB 85,000-90,000 MT (from ~72,000); Proflex 1.70-1.725 million sq m.
IPO proceeds INR259.32 crores; INR137.81 crores (53%) utilised to 31 March 2026, INR7.5 crores in Q4.
demand_pricing: Order inflow Q4 about INR387-388 crores, down from INR480 crores in Q3 (per analyst); FY26 record inflow INR1,539 crores.
Bid pipeline cited at about INR1,000-1,100 crores across sectors; domestic inquiries in last three months exceeded the prior remaining part of the year.
Export order closures slowing: US cycle time rose from 6-8 weeks to 12-16 weeks amid US inflation and cost pressures.

Steel prices rose about 20%+ in the last quarter (cited INR49,500/t to INR58,500/t); fixed-price contracts with 6-12 month execution; 80-85% of raw material is covered at order booking, 15-20% left open for non-standard items.
New orders being quoted at higher prices; price not locked until advance received. Export freight: a USD 2,000 war surcharge added; cushion built into quotes.
Export realisation about INR2.3-2.7 lakh/t vs domestic about half, driven by US bought-out items costing INR1-2 lakh/t and freight/duties.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see FY27 EBITDA margins given the geopolitical situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide, citing steel price swings (+20% in a quarter), uncertain freight and FX; it will wait at least one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Export target at least INR300 crores in FY27 (vs INR165 crores) per Malav Patel; later cited INR275-300 crores and about 10,000 tonnes; US order closures have slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 volumes grow only ~8% vs ~15% expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material and steel mill disruptions in March (two major suppliers shut, gas shortages); management estimated 10-15% volume lost to the war.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any signs of demand slowdown in PEB?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reports no slowdown in inquiries; warehousing and a gigafactory project cited as ongoing demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the forex loss and what drove the margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: INR3.83 crores is an unrealised translation loss at INR94.78/USD (from INR89-90 post-war); other drivers were export duty, sea freight and US transport costs (INR42-45 crores) and steel price rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% tariff cut passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly; the contract has a tariff sharing clause, so the company keeps part of the benefit and the customer gets part.

risks_watch: Margin visibility: no FY27 margin guidance; steel prices, freight, and FX remain uncontrolled, with 15-20% of raw material open per order.
Sanand 20,000 MT expansion commissioning targeted Q2 FY27; Proflex US units also due Q2 FY27.
Working capital: operating cash flow about negative INR36 crores in FY26 as cash purchases and creditor payments used IPO GCP funds; receivables rose.
Export order conversion slowing (US lead times 12-16 weeks); potential customer deferrals while prices fall.
Supply chain concentration: reliance on one steel supplier when two major mills were shut in March 2026; gas availability constraints.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and order book, but cautious and evasive on margins, citing uncontrolled steel, freight and FX inputs. Management repeatedly declined to give margin or quarterly guidance and asked investors to assess full-year performance.
key_quotes: We therefore encourage our investors to assess our performance on a full-year basis rather than a quarter-by-quarter.

Problem is you can cover with all your calculations you can't go beyond 80% to 85%. 15% remains open.
